title: TRAIGA
summary:
TRAIGA, or the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act, is a state law regulating the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems in Texas. Sponsored by Representative Giovanni Capriglione, the Act establishes a framework governing certain uses of AI, outlines prohibited uses, and creates obligations on state government entities. TRAIGA was signed into law on June 22, 2025, by Governor Abbott and took effect on January 1, 2026.

The law applies to AI developers and deployers that conduct business in Texas or whose systems are used by Texas residents. It prohibits the intentional development or deployment of AI systems to incite harm, violate constitutional rights, engage in unlawful discrimination, and produce child sexual abuse material or unlawful deepfakes.

In December 2024, Representative Capriglione introduced House Bill 1709, modeled in part on the EU Artificial Intelligence Act and the Colorado AI Act. After industry concerns, a revised proposal, House Bill 149, removed requirements for private companies to notify consumers when they interact with AI systems and to conduct impact assessments.

TRAIGA creates the Texas Artificial Intelligence Council to assist the state legislature in evaluating AI policy and oversight. The Council does not have binding rulemaking authority. The Act also establishes a regulatory sandbox program permitting approved participants to test AI systems for up to thirty-six months under reduced regulations. Only the Texas Attorney General can enforce TRAIGA; there is no private right of action. TRAIGA authorizes civil penalties up to $200,000 per violation alongside a sixty-day cure period. Safe-harbor provisions incentivize businesses to document compliance with frameworks like the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
